# Generate Markup Instead of Hand-Writing It

**Decision.** Delete six hand-written HTML pages carrying RDFa and JSON-LD, and generate both
syntaxes from a single JSON dataset instead.

**Date.** 2026-07-09 — the generator (`ef3b9f3`) and the deletion (`98fac45`) land the same day,
−1268 / +222.

## The rejected alternative, named with its failure mode

The alternative was not hypothetical. It was the working implementation, and it was thrown away:

> "The old approach hand-wrote the same data into six HTML files **twice** (RDFa in the body +
> JSON-LD in the head), so every fact lived in 2–4 places and could drift. This app makes the data
> the single source of truth and **generates** the markup."
> — Information-Systems-Modelling/lab6/app/README.md, 2026-07-09

The commit message says the same thing in eight words:

> "refactor(lab6): drop hand-written snapshot pages, generate from the app"
> — Information-Systems-Modelling, git commit `98fac45`, 2026-07-09

"Every fact lived in 2–4 places" is the diagnosis. A build with an RDFa `property` in the body and a
JSON-LD key in the head is asserting the same triple twice, in two syntaxes, in one file — and a
seventh page would have made it worse. See [[linked-data-publishing]].

## What replaced it

`lab6/app/data/*.json` holds the instances; one renderer emits RDFa, JSON-LD, the SSR responses and
the static `dist/` build. `src/rdf/vocabmap.js` extends the same rule to the documentation *about*
the output — the `VOCAB MAP` provenance comment on each page is produced by walking that page's own
graph, so it cannot go stale. The general form is [[single-source-of-truth-generators]], and the
vocabulary rule it applies is [[schema-org-first-custom-vocab-fallback]].

## Why this commit is the most unusual in the source set

`98fac45` **deletes a superseded version**. Across all fifteen source repositories, that happens
essentially nowhere else: the standing habit is [[keep-the-superseded-version-in-tree]], and
`Information-Systems-Modelling` is itself the corpus's four-way champion of keeping things — a dead
nested Angular scaffold, an orphaned 557-line `instances.ttl`, byte-identical `ontology.ttl` copies,
and three whole superseded backends under [[forward-copy-lab-progression]].

The same author, in the same repository, in the same fortnight, both kept everything and deleted
something. Per §10 of this wiki's schema that is a **finding about the practice, not a contradiction
to resolve**: the deletion happens precisely where keeping the old copy would have *reintroduced the
bug* — a stale hand-written page still serving stale triples is worse than no page. Where the old
version is inert, it stays.

## Costs and open threads

- The hand-written pages are gone from HEAD, so the "before" is only reachable through git history.
  That is the trade the deletion makes deliberately.
- The generated deliverable, `dist/`, is **gitignored and untracked**, while `lab6/README.md` calls
  it the thing to inspect. A reader cloning the repo gets the generator and not the output —
  [[documentation-drift]].
- `verify_jsonld.py` was deleted in the same commit, replaced by `scripts/validate.py`.

- **TODO:** whether RDFa and JSON-LD had *actually* drifted before the rewrite — and whether

  README states drift as a *risk* ("could drift"), not as an observed event. `confidence: low` on any
  claim that a real divergence occurred. Do not assert one.
